name: Skruuvi
description: Skruuvi is a Finnish trick-taking card game for four players, a descendant of the Russian game Vint and a distant cousin of Bridge. It features bidding, misère contracts, and card exchange between partners.

overview.description: Skruuvi is a Finnish trick-taking card game for four players, a descendant of the Russian game Vint and a distant cousin of Bridge. It features bidding, misère contracts, and card exchange between partners.

history.origins:
Country/Region of Origin: Finland (game developed and played in Finland); ancestral game Vint from Russia.
Time Period: Late 19th century (Vint introduced to Finland); Skruuvi codified by 1940s.
Historical Development: Descendant of the Russian game Vint; when Vint was introduced to Finland in the late 19th century it was known as Skruv-Whist (Swedish) and Skruuvi (Finnish); rules diverged and were codified in the 1940s.
Cultural Significance: Played in Finland as a niche hobby; Helsingin Suomalainen Klubi organizes annual Toro Skruuvi tournament.
timeline: Modern Era: Continues to be played worldwide
